title: Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan
summary: Prepare animals for rapid movement before noise, heat, smoke, panic, and congestion make handling unsafe.
content: Field sequence: Assign carriers, leads, pens, handlers, destination, feed and water, identity, medicines, and an early trigger for animals that require more loading time. Assess heat, smoke, floodwater, injury, escape, aggression, and disease risks before handling for “Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan”. Use species-appropriate restraint with the least force and keep animals separate when stress or disease requires it for “Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan”. Provide clean water, suitable feed, shade or warmth, ventilation, rest, and a dry waste-controlled area for “Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan”. Label carriers or pens and record identity, owner, medicines, feeding, elimination, behaviour, and destination for “Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan”. Escalate early to a veterinarian, trained handler, authority, or rescue service for injury, poisoning, breathing trouble, birth complications, or uncontrolled behaviour for “Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan”. A frightened or injured animal may bite, kick, crush, scratch, or flee; protect people without abandoning welfare in “Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan”. Do not give human medicines, unfamiliar feed, or improvised doses unless a veterinarian has directed them in “Wildfire pet and livestock loading plan”.
